blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your Southbank home? We break down the costs per square metre, planning permits and tips to save money in 2026.
body: Home extensions are a popular way to add space without moving out of your neighbourhood. In Southbank, where real estate is prime and block sizes vary, a well-planned extension can significantly increase your property's value. But how much does it actually cost in 2026? The answer depends on several factors: size, material choices, site access and council requirements. On average, a single-storey extension in Melbourne's inner suburbs ranges from $3,500 to $6,000 per square metre, with Southbank often on the higher end due to complex site conditions and stricter heritage overlays.

Before you start, check with the City of Melbourne council about permits. Southbank falls under the Melbourne planning scheme, which may restrict building height, setbacks and facade changes. A professional building surveyor can help you navigate these rules. If your property is in a heritage overlay, expect additional costs for specialised materials and longer approval times. BuildCare recommends budgeting an extra 10–15% for unforeseen council conditions.

The single biggest factor is the type of extension. A rear ground-floor addition is generally cheaper than a double-storey or a side infill. A standard rear extension with a new kitchen and living area typically costs $120,000 to $250,000. A full second-storey addition can run from $400,000 to $700,000, especially if it requires underpinning the existing footings. In Southbank, many townhouses have party walls, which can complicate structural work and increase costs.

Material choices also drive the price. For a cost-effective option, use brick veneer walls, standard timber windows and laminate benchtops. Mid-range choices include cladding, aluminium windows and engineered stone. High-end finishes like render, double-glazed frames and natural stone can add 30–50% to your budget. BuildCare always provides a detailed material schedule so you can decide where to invest for the best return.

Labour and trade availability affect costs too. With ongoing demand in Melbourne, good builders are booked months ahead. You'll pay a premium for last-minute work. To get the best price, plan your extension at least 6 months in advance and lock in a fixed-price contract that covers all trades. BuildCare offers this as standard – no surprises, no progress claims that blow out.

To save money, consider a design-and-build package where the same company handles design, permits and construction. This eliminates coordination problems and reduces fees. Also, excavate and pour concrete in summer when weather is reliable. Winter concrete requires additives and longer curing, adding cost. Finally, get at least three quotes from reputable builders in Southbank. Compare not just the total price but the scope of works. A cheap quote might lack important inclusions like demolition, landscaping or council fees.

blogPosts.title: Building a Childcare Centre in Victoria – Costs and Regulations 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about developing a childcare centre in Victoria, from Building Code requirements to cost estimates and site selection.
body: Childcare centres are in high demand across Victoria, especially in growing suburbs like Dandenong, Mount Cottrell and Armadale. If you're considering developing one, you need to understand the strict regulations and significant investment required. BuildCare has delivered several childcare centres and knows the ins and outs. The first step is finding a suitable site: it must be zoned appropriately, have good street access and be large enough for classrooms, outdoor play areas and parking.

The National Construction Code and the Education and Care Services National Law apply to all childcare centres in Victoria. This means you need fire safety systems, accessible amenities, compliant playground surfaces and adequate supervision sightlines. The building must also meet energy efficiency standards and ventilation requirements. BuildCare works with specialist consultants to ensure every centre passes the rigorous approval process without delays.

Costs vary widely based on size, location and finish. A typical two-storey childcare centre with eight classrooms, a rooftop play area and underground parking can cost between $3 million and $5 million. Site preparation – demolition, soil remediation and services connection – can add $300,000 to $600,000. In areas like Armadale where land is expensive, the total project cost may exceed $6 million. However, the return on investment can be strong with long waiting lists in many suburbs.

Funding options include bank loans, government grants (such as the Community Child Care Fund) and private investment. Some councils offer incentives for new childcare centres in underserved areas. BuildCare can help you prepare a business case to secure financing. We also handle all council applications, which typically take 4–8 months. Allow extra time for VCAT appeals if the application is contested.

Construction timelines are usually 12–18 months from start to finish. Delays often occur during the basement and structural steel phases, so a realistic schedule is crucial. BuildCare uses a detailed project plan with weekly milestones. We also coordinate with the future operator to ensure the fit-out matches their curriculum needs – like kitchen layouts, nappy-changing stations and outdoor shade structures.

After completion, you'll need to register with the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) and obtain a service approval from the Department of Education. Ongoing compliance includes annual fire inspections, playground audits and staff-to-child ratio monitoring. BuildCare provides a comprehensive handover manual and can recommend maintenance partners to keep your centre running smoothly.

blogPosts.title: Renovating Your Southbank Apartment – A Complete Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a Southbank apartment renovation? Learn about owners corporation rules, structural limitations and cost-saving tips for your project.
body: Southbank is known for its high-rise apartments and riverside living. Renovating an apartment here comes with unique challenges compared to a house. The first hurdle is the owners corporation (OC) rules. Many OC by-laws restrict structural changes, plumbing alterations and even floor coverings. You must get written approval before starting any work. BuildCare always checks the OC rules early to avoid costly rejections.

Structural changes are limited in apartments because walls may be load-bearing or part of the fire safety system. You can typically remove non-load-bearing internal walls, but kitchen and bathroom layouts are harder to change due to plumbing risers. A structural engineer's report is essential. Expect to pay $1,500–$3,000 for a full assessment. If you want to move a kitchen island more than a metre, you may need to reroute services, which can cost $5,000–$10,000.

Flooring is another area with restrictions. Many Southbank buildings require noise-rated floor coverings to meet acoustic standards. Carpet or approved vinyl planks are often mandatory. Tiles may be allowed but need an acoustic underlay. Bamboo flooring can be a good compromise. BuildCare has a list of OC-approved materials that save you time and frustration.

Budget wisely for an apartment renovation. A full kitchen and bathroom reno in a 2-bedroom unit typically costs $60,000–$120,000. Painting, lighting and new floor finishes add $15,000–$30,000. If you're doing a cosmetic refresh – new benchtops, splashback and appliances – budget $25,000–$50,000. Always include a 15% contingency for hidden issues like asbestos in older buildings or water damage behind walls.

Access is a logistical challenge. Trades need to use service lifts, book time slots and manage noise hours (usually 7am–6pm weekdays). BuildCare coordinates all deliveries and rubbish removal to minimise disruption. We also arrange temporary hoardings to protect common areas. Your neighbours will appreciate the professionalism.

Despite the hurdles, a well-executed Southbank apartment renovation can increase your property's value by 10–20%. Focus on creating an open-plan feel, maximising storage and updating the kitchen and bathrooms. Good design can make a small space feel luxurious. BuildCare offers free design consultations for apartment owners in Southbank.

blogPosts.title: The Cost of Building a Custom Home in Melbourne's Inner South 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the true cost of building a custom home in suburbs like Southbank, Richmond and St Kilda. Includes land costs, builder rates and hidden fees.
body: Building a custom home in Melbourne's inner south is an exciting but expensive undertaking. Suburbs like Southbank, Richmond and St Kilda have high land values and strict planning controls. A custom home project involves land acquisition, design fees, council permits, construction and landscaping. The total cost can easily exceed $1 million for a 200-square-metre home on a typical 300-square-metre block in Southbank.

Land costs are the biggest variable. In Southbank, a vacant residential lot can cost $800,000–$1.2 million depending on size and location. If you buy an existing house to demolish, add $50,000–$100,000 for demolition and site preparation. Richmond and St Kilda are similar. To save money, consider a knockdown-rebuild on a less expensive block in a nearby suburb like Albert Park or Middle Park, where land is slightly cheaper.

Builder costs for a custom home typically range from $3,500 to $6,000 per square metre for a standard finish, and $7,000 to $10,000 for high-end with architect-designed details. BuildCare offers transparent pricing with a detailed schedule of works. We charge a fixed fee for project management, not a percentage of build cost, so you know exactly what you're paying. Allow $2,000–$5,000 for soil tests and surveys before construction.

Council approvals take 3–6 months for a standard home, longer if there are heritage overlays or objections. In Southbank, the City of Melbourne may require a heritage impact assessment if your property is in a heritage area. This can add $5,000–$15,000 in consultant fees. Many homeowners also need a town planning permit for tree removal or boundary setbacks. BuildCare handles all applications and attends VCAT if needed.

Hidden costs include connecting to services (water, gas, electricity, NBN), which can be $10,000–$25,000. Landscaping is often underestimated: a basic garden with lawn and plants costs $15,000–$30,000, while a full landscape design with paving, irrigation and outdoor living can be $50,000–$100,000. Driveways, fencing and retaining walls add another $10,000–$40,000. BuildCare includes these in our initial estimate so there are no nasty surprises.

To stay on budget, prioritise your must-haves and finish later. Start with a weathertight shell (roof, walls, windows, doors) and complete interior fit-outs over time. Consider a slab-on-ground foundation instead of suspended slab to save cost. Use standard sizes for windows and doors. And always get a fixed-price contract that covers all trades and materials. BuildCare's custom home package includes everything from footings to final paint – no extras.
